مُقَبَّبٌ , applied to a house, or chamber, Having a قُبّة [q. v.] made above it. (S, O, K.) [And in like manner applied to a woman's camel-vehicle of the kind termed هَوْدَج: see 2. ―
-b2- And it is also an epithet applied to a solid hoof; meaning Round like a cupola: see مُفِجٌّ, and see the first sentence in art. قعب.] ＝
-A2- سُرَّةٌ مُقَبَّبَةٌ, (M, K, TA,) in a copy of the K erroneously written مُقَبْقَبَة, (TA,) A lean navel; as also ↓ مَقْبُوبَةٌ . (M, K, TA.) ―
-b2- See also القُبِّيُّونَ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
